source.title_on_document: When Are Combinations of Humans and AI Useful? - A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

paper_design_summary: A preregistered systematic review and three-level meta-analysis of 370 effect sizes from 106 experiments in 74 papers published January 2020 to June 2023 that report performance of the human alone, the AI alone, and the human-AI system on the same task. The outcome is task performance (accuracy, error, quality, and similar metrics) as Hedges' g, for human-AI synergy (human-AI versus the better of human or AI alone) and human augmentation (human-AI versus human alone). AI is defined broadly (shallow models, deep learning, Wizard of Oz), and tasks are split into decision tasks and creation tasks (open response); no creativity or diversity outcome is coded.

participants.who: Corpus of 370 effect sizes from 106 experiments reported in 74 papers (ACM DL, AISeL, Web of Science, plus forward and backward citation search), published January 1, 2020 to June 30, 2023. Participants in the included experiments range across crowdworkers, experts such as doctors, and students; 34 effect sizes come from creation tasks and 336 from decision tasks.
participants.quote: we identified 74 that met our inclusion criteria (see Figure S1). These papers reported the results of 106 unique experiments

ai_tool.name_model: AI broadly: shallow models, deep learning models, and Wizard of Oz systems (Lai et al. classification); not limited to generative AI
ai_tool.how_used: Mostly decision support: in more than 95 percent of the human-AI systems the human makes the final decision after receiving AI input (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5).

task.description: Mixed tasks coded as decision (choosing among options or giving a numerical value; 336 effect sizes) or creation (open response; 34 effect sizes). The paper does not report creativity or diversity scores for creation tasks; performance metrics are task accuracy, error, quality, and similar.

synthesis.search_end: Publication window January 1, 2020 to June 30, 2023; database search run July 2023 (PDF p. 10, Section 4.1.2; PDF p. 11, Section 4.1.3; Table S1, PDF p. 27)
synthesis.inclusion: Per the preregistration: an original experiment in which a human and an AI system work together on a task; reports quantitative performance of (1) the human alone, (2) the AI alone, and (3) the human-AI system; reports design, participants per condition, and the outcome SD (or enough to compute it); in English. Reviews, theory, qualitative work, commentaries, and simulations excluded; the limitations section says only peer-reviewed publications were included (PDF p. 10, Section 4.1.1; PDF p. 7, printed p. 6).

eligibility.reason: Meta-analysis (synthesis) of existing experiments; it reports no original randomized people experiment and therefore does not enter the core dataset (PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF pp. 10-12, Sections 4.1-4.2). It pools task performance (accuracy, error, quality) for broadly defined AI and does not report a separate creativity, novelty, or diversity outcome (PDF p. 7, Section 3, Limitations; PDF p. 12, Section 4.2.1; PDF p. 31, Table S2). Creation tasks appear as a subgroup of 34 effect sizes; this is not a people count, and there is no original participant sample to apply the core sample-size criterion to (PDF p. 32, Section S2.1; PDF p. 36, Table S7).

one_line_finding: Across 370 effect sizes from 106 experiments (2020 to mid-2023, AI broadly defined), human-AI systems performed worse than the better of humans or AI alone (g = -0.23, 95% CI -0.39 to -0.07) but better than humans alone (g = 0.64, 95% CI 0.53 to 0.74), and the 34 creation-task effect sizes showed synergy g = 0.19 (95% CI -0.09 to 0.48) and augmentation g = 0.52 [0.11, 0.93] (Section 2, PDF pp. 3-4; Table S7, PDF p. 36).

applied.old: Meta-analysis (synthesis); it runs no experiment of its own. It pools task performance (accuracy, error, quality) for human-AI combinations with AI defined broadly, not generative AI only, and it codes no creativity, novelty, or diversity outcome. Creation tasks (open response) appear only as a 34-effect-size subgroup of performance (PDF p. 4; Table S7, PDF p. 36). The main text does not name the creation-task studies; a search lead (unverified here) says the OSF data hold only two generative-AI creation tasks, neither scoring creativity.
